payload.because: A scope field would be the first derivation in this engine that is NOT retroactive — task_files, freshness and unregistered_sessions are each specified as covering every existing record. 136 decisions already exist with no scope, so D3 itself would be invisible to the check built to protect D3, and closing that needs hand-classification of the back catalogue. Scope also demands a judgment unavailable at log time (decisions BECOME repo-general later) and fails silently when under-scoped. Citation handles are already in the record: 150 citations across 12 initiatives, measured 2026-08-03. Deriving costs no schema change, no new capture, no judgment, and covers all 136 retroactively. Revisit scope only if the derived signal proves noisy in practice.
payload.chose: Derive repo-generality from citation behaviour — a decision cited from initiatives other than its own is repo-general — via a mechanical `cites` edge over the stable handle grammar (D<n>, BD<n>, <slug> D<n>, speed T<n>)
payload.over: Adding a declared `scope: repo|initiative` field to the decision_logged payload, with a doctor check over it

payload.because: The join nodes ARE the cross-initiative edge: a session id and a repo-relative path mean the same thing in every log that mentions them, so not scoping them is what recovers the provenance the per-initiative fold structurally drops. And deduping occurrence edges would make Phase 4 impossible — activity's task_changes renders EVERY status change in log order including repeats on one task, and its files list is first-touch-ordered, so a pair-deduped edge set cannot reproduce it byte-identically. Since 4.1/4.2 byte-identity is the GO/NO-GO for the whole initiative, the primitive has to keep per-event grain and let each query dedupe on the read side.
payload.chose: Three node families with distinct identity rules — STRUCTURAL (initiative/phase/task, from each initiative's final folded plan, slug-scoped because task ids like "1.1" repeat across most initiatives), OCCURRENCE (command/decision/note, one node per sourcing event keyed by its ulid), JOIN (session/file, deliberately NOT slug-scoped) — and occurrence EDGES kept as multi-edges, one per sourcing event, never deduped into pairs.
payload.over: A flat node table with deduped (from,to) pairs and a count attribute, which is the conventional adjacency shape and about half the memory.

payload.because: Measured on the live record, the loose grammar yields 275 tokens of which most are junk: bare <n>.<n> matches version strings (0.1, 0.7, 0.8) and the IP octet 127.0 — 20 false positives and zero true ones. Tightened, 62 tokens resolve to 22 decision edges and 11 task edges with 19 dangling. BD<n> (the most-cited family, BD22/BD16/BD9 at 7x each) names the archived pre-migration prose record in docs/harness.md, which has no nodes here — resolving it would require inference, and D3 forbids that; recording it keeps the signal without inventing an edge. The ordinal rule is not invented for the graph: felt-cost D3 round-trips to the zero-model-API-calls decision that SPEC cites by that handle, and repoGeneral's top result on this repo is that same decision, cited from record-graph and sync-client.
payload.chose: Tighten the citation grammar against measurement: bare <n>.<n> is NOT a handle (needs its slug), BD<n> and D-<label> are recorded as dangling rather than resolved, D<n> resolves to the nth decision_logged in that initiative's log in ulid order, and self-citations plus targets sorting AFTER the citing decision are dropped. Unresolved handles are carried on the citing decision node as dangling[], never silently discarded.
payload.over: The plan's looser sketch — D<n>, BD<n>, <slug> D<n>, speed T<n> matched literally, which is what produced the "150 citations across 12 initiatives" figure the initiative was scoped on.
